A7_S3_D1: ^Narrator: You settle next to Amelia while the Ichthyos and Krakenfolk run about — stealing food, chatting over the fire, and doing crafts without even looking down at their hands.
^Amelia: Well, as much as I can. That Zale guy—
^Amelia: He’s been stealing exactly two fish from my plate whenever I cooked in the past nights!
^Narrator: And today, she finally managed to keep it out of his reach. Zale scratches the back of his neck, accepting defeat.
^Zale: Alright, alright. Sorry for pulling a quick one over you. It’s just, normally we can’t try and season the fish until it’s cool, so the ones you grill always taste better.
^Narrator: Amelia turns away with a ‘hmph,’ but mutters that she’ll make more tomorrow. Zale brightens, the exchange making you laugh.
^Zale: You’ve also adjusted pretty quickly. How’s your hair and skin feeling?
^Noelle: They’re fine! I actually feel kind of refreshed now, whenever I come back from the ocean.
^Narrator: Zale plops onto the sand, eyes crinkling as he gazes out at the waves crashing by.
^Zale: Yeah, it’s pretty hard to go back to life on land, once you’re used to it.
^Zale: But make sure you don’t try to swim at night. It’s dangerous for newbies, and even the Ichthyos.
^Narrator: Stories from Saorise say that the ocean responds to the Moon, growing wild and mournful under its light.
^Amelia: Don’t worry, I won’t let her get that far.
^Amelia: I’m here to look out for you, right, Noelle?
^Noelle: (Tomorrow, I’m supposed to help the other Krakenfolk bring some supplies to the human settlement, to enter transit up the mountains.)
^Noelle: (Best to confirm the details with Saorise now, since she has time.)
A7_S3_D2: ^Narrator: After chatting about the shipment, the topic goes back to your boat, which you’ve managed to roughly patch up.
^Saorise: With any luck, we can use it to transport goods to the beach closer to the mountain trail. It’ll save us a lot of work once the packing gets tough.
^Saorise: But enough about business. You wanted to know more about Noah’s history, didn’t you?
^Noelle: Well… just about what hideouts he might’ve had. I suppose you could say that my curiosity is just due to a gut feeling.
^Saorise: Said gut feeling is what saves our lives at sea. You should be more confident in your instincts.
^Narrator: She explains that Noah did indeed use a cave off the beach as a base, but it’s been caved in over the past centuries.
^Saorise: It may take a while to find an entrance, or a safe one, at that.
^Noelle: This isn’t related to Noah, but…
^Noelle: I’ve been meaning to ask — did anyone on Thavmia regard the Krakenfolk as strange or… monstrous, at first?
^Noelle: I mean! Surely it must’ve been a shock to the first person who transformed.
^Noelle: (I hope she understands what I mean. I’m not trying to say that the Krakenfolk or other Thavma are strange by any means…)
^Saorise: Some even went as far to say that it was the Great Disaster’s curse on mankind, for the acts Noah committed.
^Saorise: But… after a bit of time, we calmed down and learned to understand and adapt.

^Saorise: The main belief that we uphold, is that this is simply another biological effect — this time, from the Kraken’s blood, rather than Thavmia’s unique landscape. With a few extraordinary abilities to boot!
^Saorise: To be honest, it connected us to some other islands, who traveled here after they experienced transformations, in hopes that we might have an answer or cure.
^Saorise: After all, Thavmia is known to some others as a place of miracles. A story, in some sense, for as long as we only existed in their minds.
^Saorise: Your home is not the only one to regard Krakenfolk as strange. However, their lack of creatures is another ‘strange’ trait as well!
^Saorise: I suppose that just goes to show that you can never be truly done learning about the world.
choicea7: ^Noelle: Both the human settlement and Ichthyos have been worried about it…
^Narrator: The past few days have been sunny and bright, but…
^Noelle: If the weather worsens, will the regular evacuations be—
^Narrator: Saorise turns towards the ocean, gaze narrowing.
^Narrator: Not a moment too soon, you too feel a change in the air — the wind is picking up, and if you crane your ears…
^Narrator: You nod to Saorise, running off to grab Amelia and haul your tent further inland.
^Saorise: Everyone, get indoors! Do not go outside until I say so!
^Narrator: Frowns and whispers pass. The water levels pinch and shove the beach.
A7_S3_D3: ^Narrator: The Great Floods are supposed to be gradual, with rain against clear skies.
^Narrator: …This is not the case today, with dark clouds that swirl against the horizon. Soon, raindrops will come bucketing down.
^Amelia: Last week’s storm didn’t start this quickly…
^Hint: Go to your sleeping tent and rest for the night.
